directives.treatmentLabel: Establish Supply Chain Diversification Across Critical Industrial Materials
directives.treatmentDescription: Establish a multi-source supply chain diversification program for critical industrial materials (steel, specialty alloys, semiconductors, rare-earth magnets, bearings) using the SCOR model with dual-sourcing, nearshoring, and qualified alternate suppliers to reduce single-source concentration and tariff/geopolitical exposure.
treatmentSteps: Map bill-of-materials for critical components and rank suppliers by concentration risk (Herfindahl index) and lead-time volatility
Qualify a minimum of two geographically distinct suppliers for each single-sourced critical material
Establish nearshore/reshore capacity for materials with >60-day ocean lead times or high tariff exposure
Negotiate buffer-inventory and capacity-reservation agreements for long-lead items (castings, forgings, power electronics)
Stand up a supplier-risk dashboard tracking on-time-in-full (OTIF), single-source count, and country-of-origin concentration

directives.treatmentLabel: Implement Capacity Reallocation to Underutilized Facilities
directives.treatmentDescription: Implement a dynamic capacity reallocation protocol that shifts production from capacity-constrained plants (utilization sustained >85%) to underutilized facilities, balancing network load against demand using sales-and-operations-planning (S&OP) and finite-capacity scheduling to absorb demand swings without capital expansion.
treatmentSteps: Instrument each plant with real-time OEE and capacity-utilization telemetry from the MES/SCADA layer
Build a multi-plant load-balancing model in the S&OP cycle ranking facilities by available standard hours and changeover cost
Qualify cross-plant tooling and process equivalence so SKUs can transfer without re-validation delays
Trigger reallocation when a plant utilization is sustained above 85% while a peer plant runs below 70%
Review network utilization variance monthly and rebalance before constraint becomes a bottleneck

directives.treatmentLabel: Deploy Equipment Condition Monitoring with Predictive Maintenance KPIs
directives.treatmentDescription: Deploy a condition-based and predictive maintenance program for critical rotating and process equipment using vibration, thermography, oil-analysis, and motor-current signatures fed to a CMMS, replacing run-to-failure with reliability-centered maintenance (RCM) and tracking MTBF, MTTR, and unplanned-downtime KPIs.
treatmentSteps: Classify assets by criticality (RCM) and define failure modes via FMEA for the top 20% of equipment driving 80% of downtime
Instrument critical assets with vibration, temperature, and motor-current sensors streaming to the CMMS/IIoT platform
Establish alarm thresholds and P-F intervals; convert reactive work orders to condition-based triggers
Train reliability engineers on spectral analysis and root-cause failure analysis (RCFA)
Track MTBF, MTTR, planned-maintenance percentage, and unplanned-downtime KPIs on a reliability dashboard

directives.treatmentLabel: Establish Factory Output Stress Diagnostics Tied to INDPRO and ISM Feeds
directives.treatmentDescription: Establish a real-time factory-output stress diagnostic that fuses internal production telemetry with external macro feeds (Federal Reserve Industrial Production Index INDPRO, ISM Manufacturing PMI, Census durable-goods orders, G.17 capacity utilization) to detect demand contraction, capacity overload, and supply bottlenecks before they degrade throughput.
treatmentSteps: Ingest INDPRO, ISM Manufacturing PMI, durable-goods new orders, and G.17 capacity utilization into a macro-signal layer
Correlate external indices against internal order-book, backlog, and OEE to calibrate lead-lag relationships
Define stress thresholds: PMI <50 (contraction), capacity utilization >80% sustained, durable-goods orders negative YoY, INDPRO month-over-month unexpected decline
Configure alerting that distinguishes demand-side contraction from supply-side bottlenecks (distinct from trade/logistics throughput)
Feed diagnostics into S&OP and capacity-reallocation decisions with documented response playbooks

directives.treatmentDescription: Detect upstream component and material bottlenecks specific to industrial production (semiconductor allocation, casting/forging lead times, specialty-steel availability) using supplier capacity signals and backlog aging, deliberately scoped distinct from the trade domain logistics/port throughput so production-side constraint and transport-side constraint are not conflated.
treatmentSteps: Instrument inbound backlog aging and supplier confirmed-vs-requested-date variance per critical component
Track ISM Supplier Deliveries Index and supplier capacity-utilization disclosures as leading bottleneck signals

Trigger pre-built mitigations (alternate qualification, buffer build, redesign for available parts) when a component crosses bottleneck thresholds
Couple findings to the supply diversification and capacity reallocation directives
